title: Left or Right Clicking any area of the auto hide panel while any widget's or the Panel's context menu is open hides the panel despite the pointer being on top of it
line: Clicking on an auto-hide panel to close a context menu no longer hides the panel under the pointer.
explanation: When a menu opens from the panel, Qt's Wayland plugin sends the panel a synthetic Leave because the menu grabs the pointer. It sends the matching Enter back when the menu closes only for xdg-shell parents, and the panel is a layer-shell surface, so it never gets one. The compositor sends no Enter either, because the pointer never left the panel's surface. So when the menu closed, PanelView thought the pointer was outside and turned auto-hide back on. The panel now remembers that the pointer is still on it if a Leave comes while one of its own popups is open, and keeps that until the pointer really leaves (a second Leave) or enters again.

commits.message:
shell/panelview: Keep an auto-hide panel shown when its menu closes

Qt sends the panel a Leave when one of its menus grabs the pointer but
no Enter when the menu closes, so clicking on the panel to close a menu
hid it under the pointer. Remember the pointer is still on the panel.

BUG: 464074

media.caption: Pure master: Konsole task menu open, then a left click on empty panel space; the menu closes and the panel hides with the pointer still on it, and stays hidden
Same steps with the fix: the menu closes and the panel stays shown under the pointer
Pure master, two tries in a row: the panel hides each time the menu is closed by clicking on it
With the fix, the same two tries: the panel stays shown

review.text: The root cause diagnosis (Qt Wayland's QWaylandXdgSurface::Popup not sending a synthetic Enter back to layer-shell parents) is solid and working around it in PanelView is reasonable for Plasma. However, the state tracking has a bug on repeated menus: after closing the first context menu by clicking on the panel, `m_containsMouse` stays `false` while `m_containsMouseBehindPopup` is `true`, so opening a second context menu without leaving the panel triggers another synthetic `QEvent::Leave` where `m_containsMouse && popupOpen` evaluates to `false` and clears `m_containsMouseBehindPopup`, causing the panel to hide when the second menu closes.
changes: Promote `m_containsMouseBehindPopup` back to `m_containsMouse = true` (and clear `m_containsMouseBehindPopup`) once the popup closes without a real leave—connecting to the popup's `visibleChanged` when setting `m_containsMouseBehindPopup` handles even quick open/close cycles before `m_unhideTimer` fires—so opening and closing a second context menu without leaving the panel still keeps it shown.
Reset `m_containsMouseBehindPopup = false` in `QEvent::DragLeave` alongside `m_containsMouse = false` for consistency with `QEvent::Hide`.

Verify the repeated-menu case (open menu -> click panel to close -> open another menu without leaving the panel -> click panel to close) and reference the upstream Qt Wayland bug in the workaround comment.
